facts.text: The hotel overlooks the sea and the Rock.
facts.excerpt: Overlooking the sea and the Rock, its Belle Époque architecture and its Eiffel dome, the signature feature of the Winter Garden, compose an exceptional setting.

facts.text: The hotel has Belle Epoque architecture and an Eiffel dome that is the signature feature of its Winter Garden.
facts.excerpt: its Belle Époque architecture and its Eiffel dome, the signature feature of the Winter Garden

facts.text: Pavyllon Monte-Carlo, a Yannick Alleno restaurant at the hotel, holds a Michelin star.
facts.excerpt: Gastronomy holds a place of honor with two of Yannick Alléno's tables: Pavyllon Monte-Carlo, a starred restaurant, and L'Abysse Monte-Carlo, a twice-starred Japanese restaurant.

facts.text: L'Abysse Monte-Carlo, a Yannick Alleno Japanese restaurant at the hotel, holds two Michelin stars.
facts.excerpt: the double Michelin-starred Japanese restaurant L’Abysse Monte-Carlo - Yannick Alléno

facts.text: The hotel has three restaurants: Pavyllon Monte-Carlo, L'Abysse Monte-Carlo and Le Limun.
facts.excerpt: 3 restaurants: the Michelin-starred restaurant Pavyllon Monte-Carlo, un restaurant de Yannick Alléno, the double Michelin-starred Japanese restaurant L’Abysse Monte-Carlo - Yannick Alléno and Le Limùn

facts.text: Gustave, the hotel bar, was conceived by interior architect Shirine Zirak in the spirit of a contemporary salon and serves creative cocktails.
facts.excerpt: Conceived by interior architect Shirine Zirak as a place for conversation and conviviality, in the spirit of a contemporary salon, it invites guests to savor creative cocktails in an elegant, hushed atmosphere.

facts.text: Hotel guests have access to the Thermes Marins Monte-Carlo wellness centre with an indoor pool, solarium, sauna, steam room, jacuzzi and fitness room.
facts.excerpt: The Thermes Marins Monte-Carlo wellness centre: indoor pool, solarium, sauna, steam room, jacuzzi and fitness room

facts.text: Stays include access to the private Monte-Carlo Beach Club with its Olympic-sized pool and beach, in season.
facts.excerpt: Access to the private Monte-Carlo Beach Club with its Olympic-sized pool, beach and beach facilities (in season)

facts.text: The Salle Belle Epoque is a reception room listed as a historical site.
facts.excerpt: A reception room listed historical site : the Salle Belle Epoque

facts.text: The Kids Room is exclusively for hotel guests during all school holidays except February, subject to conditions.
facts.excerpt: The Kids Room, exclusively for guests staying at the hotel (during all school holidays except February, subject to conditions)

facts.text: Resort privileges include free access to the Casino de Monte-Carlo.
facts.excerpt: Free access to the Casino de Monte-Carlo

facts.text: A private shuttle takes guests around the Resort.
facts.excerpt: A private shuttle to take you around the Resort

facts.text: Marcel Pagnol stayed on several occasions in the rooms that are now the Diamond Suite Pagnol.
facts.excerpt: when you hear that Marcel Pagnol himself stayed here on several occasions

facts.text: The Diamond Suite Pagnol includes a 130 square metre terrace and a kitchenette.
facts.excerpt: Diamond Suite Pagnol of 240m² including a 130m² terrace

facts.text: The Diamond Suite sea view with jacuzzi has a terrace with a private jacuzzi and a view of the old city and the Prince's Palace.
facts.excerpt: With its sun-bathed terrace, private jacuzzi and breath-taking view of the old city and the Prince’s Palace

facts.text: The Diamond Suites sea view were designed by Pierre-Yves Rochon, with Versailles parquet, Calacatta marble and mosaic floors.
facts.excerpt: Facing the Mediterranean, the new Diamond Suites sea view, designed by Pierre-Yves Rochon, offer a luminous and refined interpretation of the Belle Époque art of living.

facts.text: Sea-view Diamond Suites feature Versailles parquet flooring, Calacatta marble and mosaic floors.
facts.excerpt: Versailles parquet flooring, Calacatta marble, and mosaic floors

facts.text: The square seen from the city-view Junior Suites is named after the author of The Barber of Seville and The Marriage of Figaro.
facts.excerpt: The square that you can see from your suite is named after the author of The Barber of Seville and The Marriage of Figaro.

facts.text: Only dogs under 15 kg are accepted, with a daily supplement, and not in restaurants.
facts.excerpt: Only dogs under 15 kg are accepted (with a supplement of €60 per day - meals not included), except for restaurants.

facts.text: Parking is paid, at 55 euros per day.
facts.excerpt: Parking: €55 per day

facts.text: Nice-Monaco transfers by helicopter, taxi or door-to-door transfer are available at extra charge.
facts.excerpt: Nice-Monaco transfer service (helicopter, taxi or door-to-door transfer, extra charge applies)

facts.text: The hotel is on Square Beaumarchais, 98000 Monaco.
facts.excerpt: Hôtel Hermitage Monte-Carlo Square Beaumarchais, 98000 Monaco

facts.text: The hotel calls itself a haven of tranquility just steps from the heart of Monaco.
facts.excerpt: the Hôtel Hermitage Monte-Carlo offers a haven of tranquility just steps from the vibrant heart of Monaco

facts.text: The hotel bar has a terrace that is open in season.
facts.excerpt: Bar and its terrace (in season)
